findings.description: The conductor's `WorktreeRepointedError` from `verifiedWorktreeGitEnv`/`checkoutPinned` reaches the operator only through `prepareGraph`'s `failureSummary`, which cuts at 300 characters; with ordinary paths the problem text alone runs ~370 characters, so the `worktree repair` advice (and the `config.worktree` variant's "Remove the file…" advice) is always cut off. Catch it in `refreshConductorCheckout` and rethrow a short advice-first message, as the unlock refusal was shortened.

`startConductor` never calls `assertNoWorktreeConfig`, so in a repo whose `.git` is a gitfile (linked worktree, submodule, `--separate-git-dir`) the lock check lstats a path under a file, `worktree add` registers the checkout in the real gitdir, and `checkoutPinned` refuses it as a compromised session on every start, leaving a stray registration. Refuse the gitfile case before the prune/add with the same `isDirectory()` check.

`restoreWorktree`'s new `assertNoWorktreeConfig(repoPath)` passes its refusals up unchanged, so `pup fix` prints "Refusing to launch a session in <repo>: …" without the `No fix round was started.` (`NOT_STARTED`) ending its other pre-edge refusals carry; wrap it like `orNotStarted(() => assertTargetName(...))`.

In a project that commits a submodule, `assertNoGitlink` now refuses indexing on every launch, respawn and fix round, yet the profile compiler still emits the `## Code graph` section whenever a binary is found, so every session is told to reach for a `codegraph_explore` tool that is never connected; drop the section (or the binary) in that case so context and MCP config agree.

The conductor re-cut adds a third inline copy of "`worktree prune`, then lstat the admin dir to confirm the registration is gone" (also in `dropUncheckedWorktree` and `dropUncheckedRound`); at the AGENTS.md third-use threshold, a `pruneWorktreeRegistration(repoPath, worktreePath): boolean` beside `worktreeGitEnv` in git-diff.client.ts would hold the fact once.

`snapshotIndex` and `assertNoGitlink` borrow `INDEX_TIMEOUT_MS` (180 s, documented as the codegraph indexing ceiling) for pup's own one-file git reads, so its name and doc no longer fit two of three uses and a planted fifo `sharedindex.*` stalls a respawn, fix round or conductor start for 3 minutes; give these reads their own short, named timeout.

The comment "Inside the caller's try: an armed driver costs the conductor its graph, not its window" is stale: `graphForConductor` no longer has a try; the envelope is `prepareGraph`'s. Say "Runs inside `prepareGraph`'s failure envelope".

`graphForConductor`'s JSDoc adds "and runs only once a binary is found", which restates `prepareGraph`'s JSDoc ("It runs inside the failure envelope, once a binary is found"), a seam duplicate under the AGENTS.md Comments rule; drop it.

`prepareGraph`'s new JSDoc sentence "`pinned` answers the dirs the indexer's git is pinned to" is unclear and omits that `pinned` is a thunk called once a binary is found whose throw is caught as "no graph"; say so plainly.

The gate's pinned `read-tree --reset -u` still loads the existing index from the session-writable `$GIT_DIR/index` in the admin dir; a session racing to drop an index with skip-worktree entries between `worktree add --no-checkout` and the read-tree could keep chosen committed files out of the measured checkout (git internals, unverified). The old unpinned read-tree read the same index; running the gate's read-tree with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` under the private mkdtemp root would close it.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer read only conductor.service.ts, conductor.test.ts and codegraph.client.ts (4 tool calls) and said the other 18 files, docs/conventions/general.md and naming.md, and decision 101's format went unreviewed. Conventions coverage this round is partial.
Skipped review-context (no CI, infra, protocol or settings surface was touched) and review-spec (the PR names no closing issue or spec source).
